import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## What this is

A way to point any `omp`, `claude`, or `codex` shell — running in any
directory, on any of your workspaces — at Papercusp's MCP server. Plugin
tools (Repomix, GitNexus, Firecrawl, Phase 9 spawn primitive, …) and
built-ins (intel:*, artifacts:*, …) all become available. The agent
picks the workspace per call.

This is the opposite of the orchestrator's per-spawn URL: instead of
locking the agent into one (workspace, harness, role, run, spawn), the
agent gets superuser access and chooses workspace per tool invocation.

<Aside type="caution" title="Threat model: friction, not enforcement">
Loopback alone can't tell a user-shell agent apart from a
papercusp-spawned agent — both run on the same machine, same user,
same loopback. Superuser requires a bearer token from
`~/.papercusp/superuser-token` (mode 0600). A spawned agent that wants
to escalate its gates can `cat` the token file. Same way it can
`rm -rf` your home directory.

Superuser is for *honest* user shells, not for *enforced* isolation.
For real isolation, run shell-omp under a different OS user with file
ACLs that prevent the orchestrator user from reading the token.

(The orchestrator-spawned path has a separate envelope — see
[Spawn-URL signing](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/spawn-signing). Forging a
worker URL into operator-tier fails the HMAC verifier; pasting the
superuser token into your own shell does not, by design.)
</Aside>

## One-time setup

```bash
$ apps/operator/scripts/install-standalone-mcp.sh
✓ Minted ~/.papercusp/superuser-token (mode 0600)
✓ Merged 'papercusp-su' into ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json (mode 0600)
✓ Installed ~/.local/bin/psu (tracked picker launcher)
✓ Endpoint responded 200
```

The script:

1. Mints a random token — 24 bytes of `/dev/urandom` (192 bits of
   entropy) base64url-encoded into a **32-character** string (not 32
   bytes of token entropy). Only on first install — a re-run **reuses**
   the existing token so live shells keep working. (The on-disk reader
   only sanity-rejects tokens shorter than 16 chars.)
2. Writes it to `~/.papercusp/superuser-token` (mode 0600, owned by you)
3. Registers the `papercusp-su` MCP server for OMP
   (`~/.omp/agent/mcp.json`) and Claude Code (`~/.claude.json`), each
   with the operator URL + `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
4. Renders the per-client playbooks into `~/.papercusp/` and installs the
   `psu` launcher (plus the `ptool` defineTool CLI) into `~/.local/bin`
   (see [below](#the-psu-launcher-and-playbooks))
5. Verifies the operator is running and accepts the token

Re-run any time to refresh the playbooks and launcher — it **reuses** the
existing token, so live shells keep working. To rotate the token
deliberately, delete `~/.papercusp/superuser-token` first, then re-run;
the operator picks up the new token without restart (file mtime triggers
a cache refresh). Add `--profile=power` for the power-engineer subset.

## The `psu` launcher and playbooks

The MCP registration above makes the SU tools *available* to a raw `omp`
/ `claude` shell; a second layer — the **engineer-collaborator
playbook** — teaches a shell how to use them. That layer is delivered by
a single launcher, **`psu`** (the older `omp-su` / `claude-su` /
`codex-su` wrappers are retired). Plain `omp` / `claude` / `codex` stay
vanilla; only `psu` loads the playbook.

`psu` records a tracked `/adv` session, then execs the **raw** agent CLI
with the playbook + the `papercusp-su` MCP + the right per-client flags
assembled per launch (`buildLaunchSpec`):

```bash
psu                                                          # interactive picker
psu --no-picker --agent=claude --harness=papercup --no-plan  # scripting
psu --resume                                                 # resume a tracked session
```

| Agent | Playbook injection |
|---|---|
| `omp` | `--append-system-prompt ~/.papercusp/<profile>-collaborator.md` (+ `-e ~/.papercusp/papercusp-coord.ts` for coordination) |
| `claude` | `--append-system-prompt-file ~/.papercusp/<profile>-collaborator.claude.md` |
| `codex` | a per-session `CODEX_HOME` whose `AGENTS.md` *is* the playbook |

**One base, per-client overlays.** The shared base playbook
(`prompts/papercusp-su-<profile>.tools.md`) carries all client-neutral
guidance. The client-specific task/workflow tooling — which differs by
client (OMP `todo_write` / `omp:sessions`; Claude Code `TodoWrite` /
`Task`; Codex `update_plan`) — lives in a small overlay
(`papercusp-su.{omp,claude,codex}.md`) that is spliced into the base at a
`<!-- PAPERCUSP-SU:CLIENT-TOOLING-OVERLAY -->` marker.
This keeps one source of truth for the base and prevents, e.g., OMP-only
"don't use the Claude task tools" guidance from landing in the Claude or
Codex playbook.

**Codex is special.** Codex has no `--append-system-prompt`; it injects
instructions through `AGENTS.md` within its `CODEX_HOME`. So for a Codex
launch `psu` mints a dedicated per-session `CODEX_HOME` whose `AGENTS.md`
*is* the playbook and whose `config.toml` registers the `papercusp-su`
server with the bearer supplied at launch — so plain `codex`
(`CODEX_HOME=~/.codex`) never sees the server, and the token is never
written into shared config.

Re-run `install-standalone-mcp.sh` (optionally `--profile=power`) any
time to refresh the playbooks and the launcher.

## How the request flows

```
omp shell anywhere on the box
  └─ reads ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json
  └─ POST http://localhost:3070/api/mcp?superuser=1
       Authorization: Bearer <token>
       Accept: application/json, text/event-stream

operator
  └─ /api/mcp route detects ?superuser=1
  └─ checks: loopback origin + bearer matches superuser-token file
  └─ on failure: tool-shaped error from tools/call (`request_rejected: superuser_invalid_bearer`).
  │  (initialize + tools/list remain open per MCP spec; the gate fires at dispatch.)
  └─ on success: builds spawn ctx { isSuperuser: true,
                                    workspaceId: '*',
                                    role: 'operator', ... }

projected-tool dispatcher
  └─ ctx.gateBypass (from isSuperuser) → bypass role allowlist
  └─ ctx.gateBypass (from isSuperuser) → bypass capability gate
  └─ ctx.gateBypass (from isSuperuser) → bypass quota window
  └─ tool runs
  └─ tool_invocations row recorded with role='operator',
     run_id='<uuid>' (fresh per request),
     spawn_id='ephemeral-<hex>', window_key='run:<uuid>'
```

## Workspace switching

The endpoint URL is workspace-agnostic. Tools that need a workspace
take a `workspace` argument; the dispatcher uses `args.workspace ??
ctx.workspaceId`, and `ctx.workspaceId` defaults to `'*'` in superuser
mode.

To discover what workspaces exist:

```typescript
papercusp:list_workspaces()
// → { workspaces: [
//      { slug: "default", harnesses: ["sheets","papercup-org"], lastActiveTs: 1778... },
//      { slug: "scratch", harnesses: [], lastActiveTs: 1778... }
//    ],
//    defaultWorkspace: "default" }
```

Then any subsequent call:

```typescript
intel.spawn_tree({ harness: "sheets", workspace: "default", limit: 50 })
orchestrator.spawn({ workspace: "default", harness: "sheets",
                     role: "worker", featureId: "F-FILL-001",
                     chunkId: "C-1" })
```

Tools that don't care about workspace (`repomix.pack`,
`fetch_plus.fetch_clean`, `firecrawl.scrape`, `gitnexus.list_repos`)
ignore the missing `workspace` arg — they're path-driven or URL-driven.

### Scoped-superuser clamp (default OFF)

Everything above describes the default behavior, where an unresolved
superuser workspace silently becomes the cross-workspace wildcard `'*'`.
With the `papercusp-scoped-superuser-clamp` flag **ON** (it defaults
**OFF** — a reversible kill-switch the owner flips after an attended
verification), a superuser session must either resolve to a **concrete**
workspace or **explicitly** opt into unscoped god-mode via
`?workspace=*` / `?all_workspaces=1`:

- An **unresolved** workspace is no longer silently promoted to `'*'`;
  it's rejected with `scoped_superuser_workspace_unresolved`.
- A **scoped** session (concrete `workspaceId`) is confined to its
  workspace. A `crossWorkspace` tool that isn't on the read-only
  scoped-safe allowlist is denied with `workspace_forbidden`; `harness:
  'all'` / `harness:'*'` (the global escape) and a per-call `harness`
  that escapes the session's pot are denied with `harness_forbidden`.
- Opting in with `?workspace=*` / `?all_workspaces=1` is the deliberate
  cross-workspace admin path that lifts the clamp.

## What's NOT bypassed

These still apply to superuser:

1. **Per-tool input validation** — invalid args still return
   `invalid_input` 400.
2. **Per-tool timeout** — long-running tools still get killed at the
   tool's `timeoutSec`.
3. **Workspace requirement on first-party tools.** Most first-party
   tools (`harness:*`, `tasks:*`, `messages:*`, …) need a concrete
   workspace to open a PG transaction. Pass `?superuser=1&workspace=<slug>`
   in the URL — the default `workspaceId='*'` doesn't satisfy them. The
   projected wrapper throws `UnauthorizedToolError`, which the dispatcher
   codes `unauthorized` (HTTP 401, **not** `handler_error`/500), with the
   message `built-in tool "<name>" requires a workspace-scoped call —
   this session has no workspace transaction. Scope the session to a
   workspace, or pass a per-call workspace where the host/tool supports
   one.`

4. **Transport-level server-side deadline.** Independent of the per-tool
   `timeoutSec` kill, every call also gets the transport deadline
   (`PAPERCUSP_MCP_DEADLINE_MS`, default **55s**, under the 60s
   `maxDuration`). A tool that exceeds it returns a clean
   `request_timeout: tool "..." exceeded <ms>ms (still running
   server-side...)` to the client — the tool keeps running server-side.
   Pass a `_meta.idempotencyKey` to make a retry replay the result once
   it completes instead of re-executing.
5. **Power-profile narrowing (when `?profile=power`).** The power profile
   narrows **both** the advertised catalog *and* the callable set: a
   `?profile=power` (or `x-papercusp-profile: power`) superuser session
   that names an engineer-only (Group A) tool is rejected with
   `tool_not_available_for_profile: "<tool>" is not available in the
   power-engineer profile`, mirroring the `tools/list` filter so a
   direct-name call can't bypass the listing restriction.

What **is** bypassed: role allowlist, capability gate (the dispatcher's
`isSuperuser` short-circuits in both), per-window quota, and the
spawn-URL signature check (superuser has its own bearer envelope).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `request_rejected: superuser_invalid_bearer` on `tools/call` (and an empty `tools/list`) | Token mismatch, token file missing, or `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header not sent | Re-run `install-standalone-mcp.sh`; check the header is set in `~/.omp/agent/mcp.json` / `~/.claude.json` |
| `request_rejected: superuser_non_loopback` | Request didn't originate from loopback (127.0.0.1 / ::1 / localhost) | Call the operator over loopback |
| `unknown_tool` 404 | Plugin didn't load | `curl /api/plugins/host/refresh` to see load errors |
| `harness_required` / `workspace required` from a tool | Tool needs a real workspace/harness; `*` doesn't work for it | Pass `workspace: "default"` (or other slug from `list_workspaces`) explicitly |
| `unauthorized` 401 (`built-in tool "..." requires a workspace-scoped call`) | A first-party tool needs a workspace tx and the session is unscoped (`workspaceId='*'`) | Pass `?superuser=1&workspace=<slug>` (or a per-call `workspace` arg) |
| `request_timeout: tool "..." exceeded ...ms` | Tool ran past the 55s transport deadline (`PAPERCUSP_MCP_DEADLINE_MS`); it keeps running server-side | Retry with the same `_meta.idempotencyKey` to replay the result, or raise the env deadline |
| `tool_not_available_for_profile` | A `?profile=power` session named an engineer-only (Group A) tool | Drop `?profile=power` (full operator surface), or call a power-profile tool |
| `scoped_superuser_workspace_unresolved` | `papercusp-scoped-superuser-clamp` is ON and the session resolved to no workspace | Pass `?workspace=<slug>`, or opt into god-mode with `?workspace=*` / `?all_workspaces=1` |
| `workspace_forbidden` / `harness_forbidden` | Clamp is ON and a scoped session tried to span workspaces, use `harness:'all'`, or escape its pot | Use an unscoped (`?workspace=*` / `?all_workspaces=1`) session, or name a concrete in-scope harness |

## Telemetry

Every superuser tool call writes a `harness_shared.tool_invocations`
row with:

- `role = "operator"`
- `run_id = "<uuid>"` — a fresh per-request UUID, **not** a fixed
  `"standalone"` papercup (the shared papercup was dropped to avoid a
  cross-cancellation hazard)
- `spawn_id = "ephemeral-<random hex>"`
- `window_key = "run:<uuid>"`

Quota is bypassed for superuser, but the invocation row is still
recorded — the stable marker for superuser activity is the `ephemeral-`
`spawn_id` prefix.

## Revoking access

```bash
$ rm ~/.papercusp/superuser-token
```

The next `tools/call` is rejected with `request_rejected:
superuser_invalid_bearer` (and `tools/list` returns an empty catalog).
To replace it with a fresh token instead, delete it and then re-run
`install-standalone-mcp.sh` (a plain re-run reuses the existing token).
